title.narrative: Supporting the most vulnerable groups in Deir ez-Zor and rural Daraa with Livelihood activates, food vouchers, and appropriate protection activates

description.narrative: ltpgtThirteen year-long crisis followed by devastating multiple earthquakes that hit parts of Syria in February 2023 has exacerbated the severity of existing humanitarian needs in Syria. Long years of conflict have raised the population’s vulnerability to the impact of this disaster with many people having lost their jobs and businesses.lt/pgtltpgtExecution of the project activities will improve livelihoods opportunities and support the resilience of extremely vulnerable people through distribution of food vouchers and protection sessions.ltbrgtThe target areas are ltbgtGhabagheb in rural Dara"a and Deir-ez-Zor.lt/bgtltbrgtThe target sectors of this program are as following:ltbrgt1- ltbgtEarly recovery and livelihoodslt/bgt (strategic Priority two):ltbrgtThe dire economic situation and high inflation have weekended the population’s coping mechanisms, deteriorated access to livelihoods, ability to meet basic needs and the availability and affordability of services. These have resulted in high unemployment rates and risks related to resilience and social cohesion of communities.ltbrgtThe activities under this sector will be:ltbrgt- Vocational Training: Activity main goal is to provide affected families in target areas with vocational training courses to enable them to have an honorable source of income to help their families and other society war affected members taking into consideration protection main streaming and gender equality, through conducting vocational training sessions which designed based on market study.ltbrgt- Micro grants business: Skilled project participants will receive life skills and business training conducted by external trainers as well as tools and equipment in different types of projects agriculture, industry or services, to help them to start their own project.ltbrgtIn this sector 130 H.H will benefit from VT activity and 75 H.H from Small Grants.ltbrgtlt/pgtltpgt2- ltbgtFSAlt/bgt (strategic Priority two):lt/pgtltpgtFood insecurity is contributing to rising mortality and morbidity, including increased rates of malnutrition and increased humanitarian needs. Most of Syrian Governorates have gone from acceptable to stress Global Acute Malnutrition (GAM) levels.ltbrgtlt/pgtltpgtPriorities will be given to targeted beneficiaries from this activity will be as follows:ltbrgt- Families with children 6-23 months at risk of acute malnutrition or stunted. ltbrgt- Families with acutely malnourished pregnant and breastfeeding women and girls. ltbrgtlt/pgtltpgtThe aim of this activity is to provision of 5320 food voucher in monthly basis to the most vulnerable 665 families (165 families in Ghabagheb /rural Darr'a and 500 families in Deir-ez-Zor in coordination with WFP focal point) in the target areas throughout eight distribution rounds.ltbrgtlt/pgtltpgtltbgt3- Protectionlt/bgtltbrgtGBV risks: Women and girls in Syria already faced ever-increasing risks of GBV and reduced opportunities to live in a place they consider safe.ltbrgtActivities:ltbrgt- 50 Awareness GBV session 35 sessions in Deir-ez-Zor and 15 in Ghabagheb. ltbrgt- Provision of 60 unstructured PSS and PFA sessions activities to beneficiaries with the objective to respond to different needs of vulnerable groups.ltbrgt- Provision of 30 structured sessions activities to beneficiaries with the objective to respond to different needs of specific vulnerable groupsltbrgtlt/pgtltpgtltbrgtAll activities of this program from various sectors will be complementary to the rest of the GOPA-DERD’s programs implemented in the target regions through beneficiaries referring system according to their needs, which this program provides in order to secure an integrated service for beneficiaries from all sectors.ltbrgtlt/pgt
